item: Launcher parity: macOS libmalloc abort lines as whole-line templates; the stderr filter checked under four awks and without /proc; a Windows server wrapper that records the exit status and fatal-error headers
summary: macOS: the lines carry program name, pid, thread and an object address, so 13 sourced tails (libmalloc malloc_common.c / malloc_printf.c / magazine_*.c) are matched as ONE ERE over the whole line in the launcher's awk and the reader, variable parts limited to name characters/digits/hex; a 200-char cap; a test pins launch.sh's copy equal to the reader's. musl: nothing to add (mallocng assert is a_crash, hlt, no message; documented in code). The filter's record is identical under mawk, gawk, one-true-awk (the macOS lineage) and busybox awk, and the pid-file sweep and null boot id are tested with the /proc paths turned off (the macOS paths). Windows: scripts/launch_server.ps1 passes every stderr line through, records the 5 Python fatal headers and the server's signed exit status with its pid (no boot id, no pid file, so nothing to sweep); launch.cmd runs it and starts the server plainly if it left no marker; the reader names NTSTATUS exit codes (values from ntstatus.h). NOT RUN on macOS or Windows: BSD tee, macOS awk 20070501, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and a real console are untested (OPEN_QUEUE).
